title: Engineering Lead
description: You'll ship agents that move money, and you'll keep the rhythm that gets them shipped. Accounts payable, accounts receivable, treasury: autonomous agents that read the invoice, match it, negotiate the discount, release the payment, and reconcile the cash. Every one of those actions runs in production with a customer's CFO watching the result. Most of what the industry calls engineering culture was written for a world where humans typed every line. That world ended. We want to build the 2026 version: engineers who work with agents as a matter of course, where the unit of work is the loop (spec, generate, evaluate, correct, ship) rather than the ticket, where code review means reviewing the evals and prompts as hard as the diff, and where a regression suite over real customer invoices is what lets us move fast on systems that touch money. Nobody has a settled playbook for this. You'll help write ours, from inside a pod. This is a player-coach role. You'll spend most of your week shipping code in one of our pods, and you'll manage the engineers day to day: 1:1s, feedback, growth, the hard conversation when it's needed. The rest goes to the delivery rhythm: pods commit to milestones in Linear, post progress daily, and review misses every Friday with the Head of Product and the CTO. You run that review and the follow-ups. The management share grows as we go from 8 engineers to 16 and beyond; this role is the natural path to Head of Engineering. You'll report to the CTO. Causa Prima is built by the team behind Taulia and backed by Creandum. What you'll do Ship as a senior engineer, 70 to 80% of your week. Take the hardest work in your pod, unblock the integration nobody wants, and review the code that touches money personally. You set the bar by clearing it in front of the team. Manage the engineers day to day. Weekly 1:1s, direct feedback, growth plans, and the honest conversation about who's ready for more scope and who's in the wrong seat. The CTO owns hiring decisions and the technical direction; the people in the pods are yours. Run the delivery rhythm. Weekly milestone commitments, the Friday review, the dashboard of committed versus delivered, and the follow-ups when something slips. Misses are discussed to learn, not to blame; your job is that they get discussed at all, with an owner and a next step. Make the loop the way we work. Specs written so an agent can execute them, evals that run before merge, review practices that treat prompts as code. The CTO owns the architecture; you own that every pod actually works this way, including the change management when they don't. Raise risk early. You know on Tuesday what won't make Friday, and so does everyone who needs to. Sit with customers. Controllers explaining why the agent's match was technically correct and operationally wrong. AP leads walking you through an SAP extension nobody documented. That's where the next milestone comes from. What we're looking for A senior engineer who likes the operational side. You've shipped production systems where mistakes cost money: fintech, payments, ERP-adjacent, enterprise B2B. You've also managed engineers, run their 1:1s and a delivery cadence, and liked it enough to want more of it while still writing code. You build with agents. You've shipped something in the last month using an agentic coding tool that saved you a week, and you can show us. Python or TypeScript in anger, and enough PostgreSQL to review a migration without asking. You've kept commitments reliable before, with numbers. Committed versus shipped, cycle time, whatever you tracked. You've followed up on slipped work without it turning into a blame exercise. Minimal process instincts. You add a ritual when it earns its place and remove it when it doesn't. A weekly review that takes 30 minutes, not 90. You can disagree with a founder and stay in the room. We hire for trust and challenge in that order. Fluent English. German or Spanish is a plus. Munich preferred, Madrid works. You'll be in both offices regularly. This is a wishlist, not a checklist. If the role excites you but you don't tick every box, we would encourage you to apply anyway. Nice to have AI agents in production, as the product rather than a feature. Depth in purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash, or scar tissue from an SAP integration. You've grown with a team through a Series A or B. Former founder or founding engineer. title: Staff Engineer
description: Staff Engineer You'll be the most senior engineer on the agents that run finance operations for our customers — designing, building, and operating the autonomous agents that handle accounts payable and receivable end-to-end. From invoice validation and dispute resolution to cross-company negotiation and cash optimization. This is an individual-contributor role at the top of our ladder: no direct reports, full technical authority over the architecture the rest of the team builds on. What you'll do Agent architecture — Design the multi-agent system: agent boundaries, event contracts, orchestration patterns, and the separation between LLM reasoning and deterministic enforcement. LLMs inform; rules enforce. You own where that line sits for every action that moves money, and the authorization gateway that makes it non-negotiable. Agentic dispute resolution — An agent that reads the claim, gathers the evidence from the PO, contract, and delivery record, forms a position, and works it to settlement — negotiating with the counterparty where that's appropriate, escalating to a human where it isn't. Deductions and short pays classified, tied to the underlying claim, and driven to resolution rather than parked in an aging bucket. Agentic dynamic discounting — Agents that continuously price early payment against the cash position on both sides of the transaction, propose terms, and execute them. Static payment terms become a negotiation that runs on its own. Matching and reconciliation — Three-way matching across purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice with configurable tolerances; cash application against bank statements and remittance advices, including partial payments and residuals; the exception paths that follow when any of it fails. Unglamorous but important: The foundation everything agentic sits on. Validation & anomaly detection — Business rule checks, duplicate and near-duplicate detection, pricing discrepancy detection, and anomaly detection across time. Precision matters as much as recall here: a false positive is a blocked supplier and an angry procurement lead. Integration framework — ERP systems first and deepest, then banking APIs, accounting platforms, Gmail, Drive, and Slack. Auth model, credential lifecycle, data normalization. Today each connector is a project; you make the next one a configuration. Compliance & security — Agents operate within a zero-trust model. You'll design how agents verify independently against source data, how outbound content is reviewed, and how the system prevents cascading failures from prompt injection. Plus the European e-invoicing mandates now landing across France, Germany, and Spain, and what EN 16931 means for the pipeline. Platform & data infrastructure — Own the primitives every agent action rests on: an append-only PostgreSQL event store with tamper-evident hash chaining for replay and audit; cryptographic signature verification on agent events and approval chains before anything external fires; the Workflow Constraint Engine that gates payments, emails, and API calls on deterministic policy, not model output; row-level multi-tenancy and tenant-scoped credentials across every data store; attribute-based authorization via Cerbos, evaluated the same way whether the caller is an agent or a human; and the MCP security layer — auth, capability-scoping, rate limiting — for external agent-to-agent access. The engineering standard — Architecture decision records, review bar, on-call, and a clear view of what we deliberately don't build. You'll write the things the next ten engineers read in week one, and you'll spend time with controllers and AP leads watching agents fail in ways no test predicted. What we're looking for 8+ years shipping production systems; currently Staff, Principal, Lead IC, or a founding engineer. You've carried an architecture through a scaling step and lived with your own decisions. Strong systems design thinking — agent boundaries, failure modes, trust boundaries, contract evolution. Money movement is not retry-safe by default and you already know why. Depth in Python and/or TypeScript in production, and deep PostgreSQL: event sourcing, row-level security, indexing tradeoffs, schema evolution under load. Hands-on experience with LLM-powered systems, agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or similar), and document AI (LlamaIndex, LlamaParse, or similar). Strong opinions about when to use an LLM vs. a rules engine vs. traditional ML — and the courage to defend them. Experience designing data pipelines, integration architectures, or event-driven systems in production. Security awareness — you think about what happens when untrusted input meets your pipeline, and about segregation of duties before someone makes you. Technical leadership without a title: reviews that teach, designs that get adopted, engineers who get faster because you're there. Effective use of AI coding tools with strong review skills for LLM integration and auth code. Domain knowledge across the purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash cycle. You don't need all three areas below, but you need real depth in one and working fluency in the rest — enough that when a controller describes an exception, you understand it before they finish: Accounts payable — PO and non-PO invoice intake, coding to GL account and cost centre, approval routing and delegation of authority, three-way matching and tolerance handling, blocked-invoice and exception workflows, duplicate detection, payment runs, payment terms and early-payment discounts, supplier master data and bank-detail verification, period-end accruals for un-invoiced receipts. Accounts receivable — invoice issuance and e-invoicing, cash application and remittance matching, partial payments, short pays and residuals, credit memos, deductions and dispute handling, dunning and collections strategy, credit limits and credit risk, aging and DSO. Procurement — requisition to purchase order, supplier onboarding and qualification, catalogues and contract pricing, goods receipt, off-contract and maverick spend, sourcing and supplier negotiation, and the handoff into AP where most of the pain actually lives. Fluency with the systems this runs on: ERPs (NetSuite, Dynamics, or the SMB stack), the sub-ledger to general-ledger relationship, and how period close constrains what an agent is allowed to do and when. Nice to have: Peppol and EN 16931 in production, or bank connectivity via ISO 20022. Cryptographic primitives in production: digital signatures, hash chaining, tamper-evident logs.
